items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: you have been mighty wonderful, Mike, I thank you so much.

ctx.x: We used to have to play this sometimes maybe three times a night, it was so asked for, the most requested tune that we had in the book, “April in Paris.” And all the students at Hamilton, I appreciate to have a few minutes to talk with you out there, and I want to let you know that this is a happy heart of finding out in the world that if you have a will, you can make it out there. And so Count Basie was that will that gave me all kinds of inspiration to be a pretty good artist today, and to do all the fills and…

Well you know we really try and, it’s an honor, the whole purpose of doing these interviews was to let some of the students that are coming along that would not have seen some of these great bands personally, get to see what some of these great artists have to say. And there is something about an oral history, about just letting you talk and be yourself on camera, that brings an aliveness to it, that a textbook doesn’t do.
